main_body: A loom frame: a wooden outer frame (rows 9-25) enclosing a woven panel of white warp threads with a red/yellow checker band, held up by two short legs below. It is drawn flat from the front.
top_band: Rows 10-12 are a brown/tan wood band (#b77246, #d59147), but it is the same wood family as the frame sides and there is no foreshortened top surface. It reads as the upper frame beam seen face-on. No distinct lighter top surface separated from a front face.
evidence: Column scan: outline row 9, wood rows 10-12 (L 130-157), grey shadow row 13, then the woven panel rows 14-19 with red/yellow checker rows 19-21, then the bottom beam rows 22-23 and outline row 25. The top and bottom beams are mirror-image horizontal wood strips of equal tone, so the frame is a flat front elevation. The top beam (about 3 rows) has the same tone as the side posts and bottom beam, and nothing shows a top face from above. The warp panel is a vertical face. The legs show no top faces, and the base beam has no visible top. Fails the frame requirement that horizontal beams show top faces.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown (#411e05) tinted toward the wood, and the near-neutral share is 0%. The candidate has 12 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and 11 colours per tile against 17-20, which is lower but not far below. The wood ramp has about 4 steps (dark brown, mid brown, light brown, tan), and the warp threads alternate white and grey with a red/yellow checker band, which gives some texture and no flat fills (0% coverage). The piece is clearly simpler than the references, with a thin palette and little grain on the wood, and the shading is shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps, so it looks thinner next to them.
